## TL;DR

Completed the docs site QA pass from the assigned task worktree. The documentation build and its index checks passed after installing the locked VitePress dependencies. Headless Playwright rendered all 29 sitemap URLs, found Authentication through local search, and confirmed a sidebar deep link reaches its target heading. The auth-less app server and the requested app routes also returned successfully without page errors. No reproducible broken link or rendering defect required a product-code change. The VitePress LLM indexer does print one warning for a section-level sidebar URL even though that URL works in the browser; I recorded it in the QA report.

## Work and rationale

I started by confirming the current worktree and task specification, then inspected the docs site package scripts, VitePress configuration, docs store, search implementation, and existing UI search tests. The user-facing manual is a separate VitePress application in `user-docs/`; the app links several help pages on `docs.repoos.org`, while its context viewer and global search also work with repository docs. That made it important to cover both the standalone site and the app shell rather than treating a successful static build as sufficient.

The first docs build failed before VitePress could run because the task worktree had no nested docs dependencies. This was an environment setup issue, not a source failure. I installed the exact locked packages with `bun install --frozen-lockfile` from `user-docs/`, then reran the build. The build rendered the VitePress pages and passed both repository-specific post-build checks: the generated LLM index check and the AI-agent guide check.

For browser verification, I started the docs dev server and drove it with headless Playwright. I read its generated sitemap, visited each URL, and checked both the HTTP response and presence of an H1. I also opened VitePress local search and queried “authentication,” then navigated directly to the Getting Started section URL used by the sidebar. Search returned Authentication results; the deep link set the URL hash, found the heading, and scrolled the page to the section. There were no browser page errors in the docs run.

I separately started `just serve-noauth 7272` from the assigned task worktree, following the requested auth-less flow. The server built the app bundle before serving. Headless Chromium visited the root and the Agents, Checks, Settings, Deployments, and Releases routes. Each returned HTTP 200 and the app emitted no browser page errors. I compared the docs destinations found in the UI source with the docs sitemap: `/agents`, `/check`, `/configuration`, `/troubleshooting`, and `/deployments-and-releases` were all present among the successfully rendered pages.

No code fix was justified by the observed results. Existing `src/ui-app/tests/search.test.ts` already covers document title/path search and content/snippet matching. The scope of this pass was verification and reporting rather than adding a duplicate test for behavior that passed in the running site. The requested human-readable result is in `docs/qa/2026-11-docs-site.md`.

## Approaches tried

- Ran the docs build before installing dependencies to distinguish a missing environment setup from a source issue. It failed with `vitepress: command not found`.
- Installed only the nested docs project’s frozen dependencies, then repeated its production build and helper checks. This passed.
- Used a headless Playwright loop over the generated sitemap rather than checking only the landing page. It verified all 29 URLs for a successful response and rendered H1.
- Tested the local search interactively in Chromium and searched for “authentication.”
- Tested the precise sidebar section URL in Chromium and confirmed its heading and browser scroll position.
- Started the auth-less app server from the task worktree and visited the app routes implicated by docs help links.

## Challenges and blockers

The task worktree initially lacked VitePress dependencies. The frozen install resolved that without changing dependency declarations. The VitePress build reports a warning from `vitepress-plugin-llms` because it tries to match `/getting-started#starting-a-new-project-as-an-agent` as a file while generating the LLM index. Browser verification shows that the URL itself is valid and reaches the intended section, so I left the useful sidebar deep link intact and documented the generator warning.

The app smoke pass was unauthenticated by design. It verified route responses and shell startup, not authenticated or populated app states. External production-domain availability was not used as proof; destinations were checked against the local docs build from this worktree.

## Key learnings

The docs project has its own lockfile and dependency installation in `user-docs/`; a freshly prepared task worktree can have root dependencies available while VitePress is still absent. For reproducible QA, build the nested project after its frozen install. The VitePress sitemap provides a practical complete route list for browser rendering checks, while local search and section anchors need direct interaction tests because successful static output alone does not prove either behavior. Finally, a sidebar section URL can work for readers even when the LLM index plugin logs a file-matching warning; the warning should be assessed against browser behavior before navigation is changed.
